svg.title: UX-10 mockup 3 · Visual and Table views of the same selected position
svg.desc: Visual and Table tree views side by side for one branched game with 5. H6 selected.

text.font-family: Noto Sans, Cantarell, DejaVu Sans, sans-serif

svg.text: UX-10 mockup 3 · Visual and Table, same game, same selected position

text.font-family: Noto Sans, Cantarell, DejaVu Sans, sans-serif

svg.text: Position: 1 H8, 2 I9, 3 I7, then the selected branch 4 G7, 5 H6. The other branch is 4 G9, 5 H9, 6 J8. Proposal mockup, dark theme.

svg.text: Selection rules when switching views (proposal, consistent with how the app works today)

text.font-family: Noto Sans, Cantarell, DejaVu Sans, sans-serif

svg.text: One selection exists, the game's current node, defined by its move path. Visual and Table are two read-only projections of it, so switching tabs never changes it.

text.font-family: Noto Sans, Cantarell, DejaVu Sans, sans-serif

svg.text: Observed: switching between the tabs left the board and the highlighted move unchanged. The graph marker and the board were identical in both screenshots.

text.font-family: Noto Sans, Cantarell, DejaVu Sans, sans-serif

svg.text: Click a node in Visual or a row in Table jumps the board to that path. The other view re-renders: Visual moves the double ring, Table ends on the new row and scrolls it into view.

text.font-family: Noto Sans, Cantarell, DejaVu Sans, sans-serif

svg.text: Selecting a fork row in Table, for example 3. I7, keeps both continuations visible in Visual as dashed off-path lines. Proposal: Table keeps the rows after the selection dimmed, so one click does not shorten it.
